subject.title: fix(slack): add 30s timeout on read WebClients, not Bolt App.client

question: Should all dedicated Slack read clients use a 30-second per-attempt default while Bolt, write, and upload clients remain unbounded?
rationale: Tests establish the implementation boundary, but maintainers must own the operational tradeoff between bounded read hangs and timeout-driven failures in slow workspaces and delivery reconciliation.

options.title: Accept the scoped read deadline
options.body: Approve the 30-second read default after rebasing and confirming every generic read-factory caller is non-mutating.

options.title: Narrow the deadline further
options.body: Apply the default only to explicitly enumerated probe, scope, and lookup clients until reconciliation tolerance is separately proven.

options.title: Keep reads unbounded
options.body: Close or defer the PR if maintainers prefer caller-owned cancellation rather than a plugin-wide read default.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped read deadline
recommendation.body: Approve the 30-second read default after rebasing and confirming every generic read-factory caller is non-mutating.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent shared Slack client-option and Bolt plumbing and have the strongest available history signal for this boundary.
